name: Proxima Centauri
why: Closest star to the Sun; motion is obvious across epochs.
look: Watch it slide west; difference mode shows a clean dipole.

name: Kapteyn's Star
note: Second fastest mover in my list; halo subdwarf
why: Extreme proper motion reveals halo kinematics.
look: Track the fast linear path and fit proper motion.

name: Wolf 359
why: Nearby flare star with strong motion.
look: Blink epochs for the moving point source.

name: Lalande 21185
why: Bright, fast red dwarf ideal for astrometry.
look: Measure centroid shift between visits.

name: Groombridge 1830
why: Very high proper motion halo star.
look: Confirm linear motion across multiple epochs.

name: 61 Cygni A
why: Historic parallax target with clear motion.
look: Compare the binary motion against catalog tracks.

name: Lacaille 9352
why: Fast southern red dwarf.
look: Track motion and photometry across epochs.

name: Van Maanen's Star
why: Nearby white dwarf with measurable motion.
look: Use difference mode to confirm movement.

name: Sirius
why: Extremely bright point source for saturation tests.
look: Inspect overflow flags and saturated cores.

name: Tau Ceti
why: Sun-like star for spectral comparison.
look: Check the 102-channel spectrum and stability.

name: Epsilon Eridani
note: Young Sun-like star with a debris disk
why: Young Sun-like star with circumstellar material.
look: Look for excess and variability in the infrared.

name: TRAPPIST-1
note: Seven-planet system; very faint in the optical
why: Faint host of seven transiting planets.
look: Use deeper co-adds and spectra.

name: Luhman 16 (WISE 1049-5319)
why: Nearest brown dwarf pair for cold-world spectra.
look: Resolve thermal emission beyond 4 microns.

name: GJ 229 A
note: Hosts a T dwarf too close to resolve at 6.15 arcsec pixels
why: Host of a T dwarf; tests resolution limits.
look: Inspect the blended core and PSF.

name: Mira (omicron Ceti)
note: Prototype Mira variable, period about 332 d
why: Prototype long-period variable.
look: Track brightness changes across visits.

name: Chi Cygni
why: Mira variable with large amplitude.
look: Compare epochs in difference mode.

name: R Leonis
why: Mira variable for light-curve extraction.
look: Measure aperture photometry across epochs.

name: T Tauri
why: Prototype young stellar object.
look: Inspect variability and spectral slope.

name: Betelgeuse
why: Extremely bright star for saturation tests.
look: Inspect overflow flags and saturated cores.

name: Orion Nebula (M42)
why: Star-forming region with dust and ices.
look: Examine extended emission and flags.

name: Barnard 68
why: Dark cloud for ice absorption studies.
look: Look for absorption features in spectra.

name: Eta Carinae
note: Massive star in a dusty nebula
why: Massive star in a dusty nebula.
look: Inspect bright core and extended nebulosity.

name: Crab Nebula (M1)
why: Supernova remnant for extended-source tests.
look: Compare extended structure across epochs.

name: Cassiopeia A
why: Supernova remnant in a crowded field.
look: Inspect extended emission and flags.

name: Sagittarius A* (Galactic Centre)
why: Crowded Galactic centre field.
look: Handle saturation and source confusion.

name: Andromeda Galaxy (M31)
why: Nearest large galaxy for extended-source tests.
look: Inspect extended disk and nucleus.

name: North Ecliptic Pole
why: SPHEREx deep field with the most epochs.
look: Use all available epochs and spectra.

name: South Ecliptic Pole
why: Southern SPHEREx deep field.
look: Use all available epochs and spectra.
